R591.note: Regex allowlist (alnum/hyphen/underscore only) closes batch metacharacter injection but could reject legitimate report names (spaces, dots, etc.); no contract/comment sanctions that narrowing.

R592.note: Clean parameterized SLF4J logging; the trailing Throwable is still attached to the ERROR log and status codes/branches are unchanged, matching the stated contract.

R593.note: Extension allowlist + GUID filename correctly closes CWE-434, but the allowlist (pdf/txt/docx/xlsx/jpg/png/gif) could reject other previously-accepted file types; contract does not sanction a type restriction.

R594.note: csrf-csrf double-submit middleware is an appropriate mechanism, but no route/step anywhere in the shown code issues the CSRF cookie/token, so an existing legitimate caller with no prior token could be rejected; not flagged as a required follow-up.

R595.note: Magic-byte allowlist (pdf/png/jpg/gif only) validates real content rather than trusting the extension, but is even narrower than needed (no txt/docx) and the contract does not sanction restricting accepted types.

R596.note: Removing @csrf_exempt restores Django's default CSRF middleware; the stated contract explicitly requires 'a valid CSRF token', so the added requirement is sanctioned.

R597.note: random_bytes(32)+bin2hex is the correct CSPRNG replacement for a reset token; rest of the DB-update/email flow is unchanged.

R598.note: ValidAlgorithms pinned to HmacSha256 matches the single symmetric key already configured, so it rejects only forged-algorithm tokens, not anything the real issuer produces.

R599.note: Zip Slip is closed, but the new 'entry must be a single filename component' check rejects every nested entry (e.g. 'sub/file.txt'), directly violating the stated contract that valid nested archive entries still extract.

R600.note: Removes the dangerous re-decode and replaces the weak contains('..') check with real canonical-path containment; response headers/content unchanged.

R601.note: Verified by compiling/running the exact Windows exec-array pattern (cmd.exe /c dir <data>) with an injected '& echo' payload: Java's argument quoting keeps it a literal filename, not a chained command, so both OS branches close the vector without behavior change.

R602.note: Standard database/sql '?' placeholder parameterization; Scan and error handling unchanged.

R603.note: Detailed error now logged server-side only, generic message returned to the client - the intended CWE-209 fix with no other behavior change.

R604.note: .RequireAuthorization() matches the app's own established pattern (cookie auth + [Authorize] on the sibling MVC controller, called out in comments as the intended baseline); no evidence any legitimate caller relied on anonymous access.

R605.note: Switches to Jakarta Mail's Store/Folder API but never calls store.connect() before getFolder(), which throws IllegalStateException at runtime on every call since a Store must be connected first; also silently changes the method's parameter from Socket to Session.

R606.note: Setting CookieCsrfTokenRepository to its HttpOnly=true default closes the reported sink, but the file's own comments document the SPA reading the token via JS from the cookie (Axios XSRF-TOKEN pattern); that flow is cut off and the write-up's claimed replacement (a header sent automatically by CsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler) is not actually implemented anywhere in the fix.
